claims.claim: No retrieved Astra card directly establishes a molecular reaction-selectivity, catalytic-cycle, photochemical-cycle, or electrochemical-cycle mechanism.
claims.basis: Search of the task-relevant topic routes and the directly relevant card families; not an exhaustive search of every source payload or external literature.

claims.claim: N33 establishes a candidate all-endotactic deterministic permanence theorem under fixed finite diagram, class, and globally bounded strictly positive measurable rates; its common-span switching corollary and periodic-orbit existence do not imply product selectivity, yield optimization, uniqueness, or attraction.
claims.boundary: Finite actual exponent-arrow diagram; positive stoichiometric class; supplied 0 < kappa <= k_e(t) <= K; endotactic essential-source condition. Delays, stochastic jumps, and unrestricted external forcing are outside the theorem.

claims.claim: N34/N50 certificate and recognizer mechanisms do not provide efficient general intervention synthesis or product-selectivity guarantees.
claims.boundary: N34 certifies/refutes supplied rational candidates and finite boxes/chains; global absorption on unbounded classes is a separate obligation. N50 completeness is conditional on the reconstructed joint-parameter affine lemma; CAD is unimplemented and no complexity bound is stated.

claims.claim: N35 gives an internally reconstructed finite-horizon stochastic confinement bound for supplied strict inward-polytope certificates under predictable bounded controls; it is not infinite survival, stationarity, or a selectivity result.
claims.boundary: Integer-complex molecular mass-action propensities; acquired compact positive polytope, strict collars uniform over allowed modes, coordinate bounds, lattice-compatible starting counts; finite-volume estimate through an exponentially long but finite horizon. Controller, acquisition, and physical actuation costs are not solved by the result.

claims.claim: N76 supplies the closest distinct stochastic-kinetics mechanism: an exact falling-factorial potential controls upward changes in the embedded event chain but not negative drift, physical-time recurrence, or selectivity.
claims.boundary: Fixed finite positive rates for the event-chain statement. Full technical note, code, logs, and original packet were unavailable in the pinned knowledge export. Fast cycle transitions and holding-time control remain open.

claims.claim: N77 warns that a common deterministic attractor does not imply uniformly tight stochastic stationary laws across a stoichiometric class; componentwise positive recurrence remains compatible with the counterexample.
claims.boundary: Counterexample summary only; full proof/code/log packet unavailable. Historical novelty is not established.

claims.claim: A cycle-resolved stochastic product-selectivity problem that turns N76 event-count control into physical-time first-passage or occupation-flux bounds is a proposed direction, not a result or priority claim.
claims.next_gate: Specify one finite driven molecular network, exact propensities, allowed intervention, competing-product observable, and a falsifiable cycle/holding-time reduction; compare against a matched baseline. Establish whether the event-count bound survives in physical time and controls the product ratio.

excluded_cards.reason: Conditional on N33 affine mechanism; spatial permanence/complex-balanced attraction, not product selectivity.
Three-gain parameter-dimension/minimality result for a seven-coordinate pullback; not catalytic reaction kinetics or a selectivity theorem.
